title: Session middleware cleanups after RF-177/RF-178: refresh short-circuit, explicit cookie strip, per-cookie copies, gate mounts
acceptance: refreshSession on POST /auth/session always resolves with refresh, even if an earlier requireSession in the same request set sessionResolved; a unit test runs refreshSession after requireSession and asserts the row is extended.
An /api/v1 after-middleware (or equivalent) removes any session-token Set-Cookie, so the no-session-cookie guarantee does not rest only on omitting returnHeaders; a test pins it.
The session gate is mounted once per request path instead of about 14 times, or the repetition is documented as intended.
The per-cookie Response copy via c.header is removed or justified (moot if no session cookie is forwarded).
conventions.md and authorization.md lines touched by #705 are re-wrapped to the file width.
nextAction: Owner triages; pairs with the standalone auth deploy (#703, #705).

evidence.summary: Final review of #705 (merged as 14d0b32) at 8a4078a: refreshSession now inherits the sessionResolved short-circuit, so a requireSession mounted before /auth would silently stop extension (safe today because index.ts mounts /auth first; no test pins it); no explicit Set-Cookie strip; docs not re-wrapped. Not blocking.
Deferred RF-177 review items: per-cookie Response copies via c.header and the session gate mounted on about 14 routers.
